thread.title: Facebook Rejects Claims In New York Times Story About User Data Abuse

author: BRIAN DEAGON
title: Facebook Rejects Claims In New York Times Story About User Data Abuse

organizations.name: facebook rejects claims in new york times story about user data abuse facebook

text:
Facebook ( FB ) replied to a New York Times article published Sunday that said it gave device makers deep and inappropriate access to data on users, saying it disagrees with accusations of data-sharing abuses.
X
Facebook's vice president Ime Archibong contends deals involving software apps and user data access were necessary.
"In the early days of mobile, the demand for Facebook outpaced our ability to build versions of the product that worked on every phone," Archibong said in a blog post Sunday. There were no app stores back then, said Archibong, who oversees Facebook's product partnerships.
"So companies like Facebook, Google, Twitter ( TWTR ) and YouTube had to work directly with operating system and device manufacturers to get their products into people's hands," he said.

Please contact customer service CLOSE The Times article said that as the company sought to become the social media leader, it gave phone and other device makers access to vast amounts of personal information on its users.
Facebook's 60 Partnerships The article said the social networking giant had data-sharing partnerships with at least 60 device makers. These included Apple ( AAPL ), Amazon ( AMZN ), Microsoft ( MSFT ) and Samsung. The agreements came over the last decade, when apps were developed to gain presence on smartphones.
To expand its reach, the company let device makers offer customers popular features of the social network. This included messaging features and address books.
It also allowed device companies access to the data of users' friends without their explicit consent. This occurred even after saying it would no longer share such information with outsiders.
Shares skidded by 0.4% to close at 193.28, during afternoon trading on the stock market today .
The company has been under intense scrutiny from regulators and shareholders after it failed to protect the data of some 87 million users that was shared Cambridge Analytica. That activity led to congressional hearings .
